We will solve this problem using integration by parts. We start by defining $u$ and ${v}^{′},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=\frac{2}{x} \\ {v}^{′}=2x\, & ⟹\,v=\int 2x\,\text{d}x={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula of integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 2x\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\,\text{d}x & =\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot {x}^{2}-\int {x}^{2}(\frac{2}{x})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-\int 2x\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-2\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-{x}^{2}+C \\  & ={x}^{2}(\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})-1)+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is an integral constant.
